findings.method: Two-proportion z-test in Python using scipy.stats.norm.cdf
findings.code:
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
df = tables['ab_test']
variant_a = df[df['variant'] == 'A']['converted'].sum()
total_a = len(df[df['variant'] == 'A'])
variant_b = df[df['variant'] == 'B']['converted'].sum()
total_b = len(df[df['variant'] == 'B'])
pooled_p = (variant_a + variant_b) / (total_a + total_b)
se = (pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/total_a + 1/total_b)) ** 0.5
z_score = (variant_b/total_b - variant_a/total_a) / se
p_value = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_score)))
